newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli government sets inflation target for '97.
newsitem.headline: Israeli government sets inflation target for '97.

text.p: The Treasury announced on Saturday that the Israeli government approved the 1997 inflation target of seven to 10 percent, a Treasury statement said.

"The government recorded the decision...that the inflation target for 1997 would be between seven to 10 percent," the statement said adding that the government took the decision at its weekly meeting on Friday.
The Treasury decided that the inflation target for 1998 would be set sometime in the first half of 1997 so it would be known before discussions on the 1998 budget began.
The Treasury also said that the target for 2001 would correspond to inflation rates of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).
Israel's inflation rate for 1996 is expected to be just above 10 percent. The inflation target for 1996 was eight to 10 percent.
